questions.stem: What is the key difference between addition and condensation polymerisation?

options.text: Addition uses heat; condensation does not
Condensation produces a small molecule (e.g., water) as a by-product; addition does not
Addition uses two different monomers; condensation uses only one

questions.explanation: In condensation polymerisation, a small molecule (usually water) is released each time two monomers join. In addition polymerisation, no by-product is formed.

questions.stem: What type of monomers are needed for condensation polymerisation?

options.text: Monomers with two functional groups (one at each end)
Monomers with only one functional group

questions.explanation: Condensation polymerisation requires monomers with two functional groups, one at each end of the molecule. These functional groups react with each other to link the monomers and release a small molecule.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a condensation polymer?
questions.explanation: Polyester and nylon are both condensation polymers. Polyester is made from a dicarboxylic acid and a diol, while nylon is made from a dicarboxylic acid and a diamine.

questions.stem: What type of bond links the monomers together in polyester?
questions.explanation: In polyester, the monomers are linked by ester bonds (-COO-). These form when the -COOH group of one monomer reacts with the -OH group of another, releasing water.

questions.stem: What type of bond links monomers together in nylon (a polyamide)?
questions.explanation: In nylon, the monomers are linked by amide bonds (-CONH-), formed when the -COOH group of a dicarboxylic acid reacts with the -NH₂ group of a diamine, releasing water.

questions.stem: Why are condensation polymers generally more biodegradable than addition polymers?

options.text: They are made from natural materials only
The ester or amide linkages can be broken down by hydrolysis with water or by microorganisms
They are thinner than addition polymers

questions.explanation: Condensation polymers contain ester or amide linkages that can be broken by hydrolysis (reaction with water). Enzymes in microorganisms can catalyse this hydrolysis, making them more biodegradable.

questions.stem: A polyester is made from a diol and a dicarboxylic acid. What does 'di-' mean in this context?

options.text: The monomer has two carbon atoms
The monomer has two of the same functional group (one at each end)
The monomer is doubled in size

questions.explanation: 'Di-' means two. A diol has two -OH groups and a dicarboxylic acid has two -COOH groups, one at each end. This allows the chain to grow in both directions.
